ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle D=90^\circ$, $\angle B=60^\circ$, $AD=6$, $AB^2=\frac{100}{3}$, $AB\perp AC$. A point $E$ is chosen on $CD$, and line $AE$ is drawn. Triangle $ADE$ is folded along $AE$ so that point $D$ falls on point $F$ on $AC$. Find: What is the length of $CD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB \perp AC$ and $\angle B = 60^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BCA = 30^\circ$,\\
which implies $BC = 2AB$,\\
hence $BC^2 = 4AB^2 = \frac{400}{3}$,\\
therefore $AC^2 = BC^2 - AB^2 = 100$,\\
leading to $AC = 10$.\\
Since $\angle D = 90^\circ$,\\
in $\triangle ADC$, where $AD = 6, AC = 10$,\\
by the Pythagorean theorem, it is found that $CD = \boxed{8}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle D=90^\circ$, $\angle B=60^\circ$, $AD=6$, $AB^2=\frac{100}{3}$, and $AB\perp AC$. A point $E$ is chosen on $CD$, and line $AE$ is drawn. Triangle $ADE$ is folded along $AE$ so that point $D$ falls on point $F$ on $AC$. What is the length of $CD$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $AB \perp AC$ and $\angle B = 60^\circ$,\\ it follows that $\angle BCA = 30^\circ$,\\ which implies $BC = 2AB$,\\ hence $BC^2 = 4AB^2 = \frac{400}{3}$,\\ therefore $AC^2 = BC^2 - AB^2 = 100$,\\ leading to $AC = 10$.\\ Since $\angle D = 90^\circ$,\\ in $\triangle ADC$, where $AD = 6$ and $AC = 10$,\\ by the Pythagorean theorem, it is found that $CD = \boxed{8}$.

The problem also gives ∠D=90°, ∠B=60°, AD=6, AB^2=100/3.
Reasoning: In triangle ABC, AB⊥AC, so ∠A=90°; also ∠B=60°, therefore ∠C=30°. This is a 30-60-90 right triangle, and AB is the side opposite 30°, AC is the side opposite 60°, so AC=AB·√3. From AB^2=100/3, get AB=10/√3, therefore AC=10. Then look at triangle ADC, ∠D=90°, AD=6, AC is the hypotenuse and AC=10. By the Pythagorean theorem, CD=√(AC^2-AD^2)=√(100-36)=√64=8. The folding condition is only an auxiliary construction and does not affect finding CD.
